purpose: An empty history is not a history.
Every prefix of a valid history is a valid history — this is how a historical question is asked.
The successor may do what it was separately granted.
THE THESIS. The successor holds the duty and must NOT inherit the power that created it.
Nor any other power the predecessor held.
A previously valid request from the replaced actor is refused.
Revoking the successor permission denies the action without deleting the duty.
An action outside every grant is refused.
A resource outside every grant is refused.
An actor with no recorded identity is refused.
A grant past its expiry is refused, with the specific code.
A request for another deployment is refused, never evaluated.
A request under another policy version is refused.
An amount inside the mandate is permitted.
The ceiling is inclusive.
One unit over the ceiling is refused, with the specific code.
Zero is an amount, not a missing one.
A budgeted authority refuses a request carrying no amount.
THE BUDGET THESIS. An amount inside the grantor’s mandate but outside the delegate’s own budget is refused.
The delegate may spend within its own smaller budget.
An unbudgeted authority is unaffected by amounts.
A history carrying budgets, ceilings and counts replays.
A delegation may not grant a larger budget than its parent holds — refused at admission.
A budgeted parent cannot delegate an unbudgeted child — otherwise a budget is escaped by dropping a flag.
The replaced actor is TERMINATED, its duty survives, its role is gone and its authorities are invalidated.
The successor is ACTIVE and holds the inherited duty.
Asked of the earlier history, the predecessor is still ACTIVE and holds its role.
An agent that was never recorded is answered honestly, not invented.
